text:
matt: Heads-up — planning a maintenance window for the APAC satellite racks (az-sat1) next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Purpose: thermal calibration + NVMe firmware rolling update. Expect soft reboots and node drains in small cohorts.
anya: put the window in calendar? Is this going to affect hosted pools or just Dedicated/Dedicated-satellite?
matt: primarily satellite-hosted pools (low-latency edge). We'll touch a few Dedicated nodes that are cross-attached for burst. Trying to avoid egregious capacity churn.
liam: how big are cohorts? we need numbers to decide pre-warmbackfill size.
matt: cohorts of 6 nodes per rack, stagger 10m apart. Total racks ~4 (24 nodes). Estimated token throughput hit ~8-12% for az-sat1 peak window.
carla: can we route traffic to eu-west fallback during the hottest parts? routing policy exists but egress costs spike. Product asked for cost estimate if we shift 10% traffic to eu-west.
liam: rough math: 10% shift for 2h => additional egress ~3TB, bandwidth egress cost ~ $0.12/GB => ~ $360. Add some VM-hour delta for warm standby ~ $200. ballpark $600.
anya: ok keep product cost-aware. Also need to flag Dedicated customers; we'll offer opt-in for scheduled isolation.
matt: plan: 1) mark node cohorts 2) run graceful drain (k8s drain + KV cache finalize) 3) soft reboot NVMe 4) verify telemetry for 30m 5) uncordon. We'll use `drain` helper:
```
# drain command pattern
./drain --pool=az-sat1-edge --cohort=cohort-2 --grace=300 --kv-seed=true
```
liam: reminder: ensure KV cache pre-seed on fallback pool to avoid cold-cache token spikes. We'll run a prime pass 20m before each cohort.
carla: will there be any transient 5xxs we need to page oncall? We should bias to degrade gracefully to smaller model for hosted API rather than return 5xx.
matt: yes fallback policy will route to `edge-compact-v1` variant for low-latency calls. That keeps API success rate high but may increase token cost ~15% for affected requests.
anya: scheduling note: this window intersects APAC peak by ~30 min — can we shift 1 hour earlier? Ops prefers 02:00 UTC to catch local night. Product: prefer earlier if possible.
liam: earlier shift triggers overlap with nightly batch jobs in az-sat1. We can move 30m earlier only. Otherwise more churn.
carla: communicate to customer success + Status page: highlight expected duration and mention fallback to compact model plus potential small latency bump.
deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance ticket created: https://tickets/repo/INFRA-2142 — cohort rollout steps attached.
matt: runbook highlights (short):
- prereq: reserve warm standby capacity + prime KV cache 20m pre-cohort
- step1: cordon cohort nodes
- step2: `./drain` (grace 300s) watch pods terminating
- step3: NVMe FW update + soft reboot (`fw_updater --slot nvme --apply`)
- step4: healthcheck: tracers, tail latency, qps, GPU temp <72C, NVMe SMART OK
- step5: uncordon + warmbackfill verification
- rollback: if >2% 5xx or >30% latency P95 regression, revert firmware via `fw_updater --rollback` and reassign tasks to fallback pool

liam: can infra cover potential burst credits if oncall needs to spin up extra capacity? we should have a burn limit to avoid surprise billing.
matt: suggest cap at $1000 burn for emergency warm-up. We'll notify finance for pre-approval.
carla: I've drafted a short Status page blurb and a customer email for Dedicated tenants with dedicated node exposure. Will send for review.
anya: one last ask — update runbook with exact node IDs. matt can you paste cohort nodes when you create the ticket?
matt: pasted in ticket INFRA-2142 but copy here:
```
cohort-1: azsat1-rack1-n[01-06]
cohort-2: azsat1-rack2-n[01-06]
cohort-3: azsat1-rack3-n[01-06]
cohort-4: azsat1-rack4-n[01-06]
```
carla: :thumbsup: ok team, I'll kick off comms after ticket final review.
liam: I'll run the KV prime scripts and keep metrics dashboards open. Ping me 15m before first cohort.
matt: thanks — creating calendar invite + posting status. Will update thread with final start time if any shift.
carla: noted. good luck and minimal surprises pls.
__note: All fields are strings or list of strings to match agents.md constraints. Thread is one continuous string with prefixed sender names.
